newsitem.title: UK: Dlr/mark nears new high but flags amid US holiday.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/mark nears new high but flags amid US holiday.

text.p: The dollar was firm in late European trade, rising to within reach of a new 40-month high against the mark, but lacking the energy for a last dash to that level with the U.S. market closed for a holiday.
Amid a lack of fresh impetus, a slightly lower-than-expected U.S. employment figure on Thursday had initially carried its mood over until today and discouraged dollar buying.

However, traders and analysts said the dollar stood its ground because the data did not herald a radical turnaround in the recent dollar bull sentiment, although it had dampened prospects of higher U.S. interest rates in the immediate future.

"The numbers don't really change the picture for interest rates. The Fed didn't change rates this week, but there is the risk that the minutes from the May 20 Fed meeting will show that they will eventually have to do something," said Rob Hayward, economic adviser at Bank America in London.
"U.S. interest rates may remain flat for some time, but the next move has definitely got to be up," he said.

Meanwhile, uncertainties surrounding European monetary union should also support the dollar against the mark as the market braces for the unveiling of the French public finances audit and the German budget, both due later this month, analysts said.
"It's clear both the French and German budget deficits are overshooting and that they are going to have to interpret the EMU criteria in quite a loose fashion," Hayward said.
The dollar was at the session high of 1.7560/65 marks at 1540 GMT, just a shade below its multi-year high of 1.7566 hit on Thursday. It was at 1.7510/15 in late Europe yesterday.

It was not at heights quite as spectacular against the yen although it was firmer than it was on Thursday, trading at 113.77/87 against 113.42/52. But the yen spiked up to near a 20-month high against the mark, trading at 64.78/81 per mark against Thursday's 64.85/87.
The near-term outlook for dollar/yen was somewhat different to that for dollar/mark, analysts said, adding that they expected the U.S. currency to tread water against the yen or perhaps slip lower.

"The issue of Japan's current account balance will emerge again with the Japanese data coming out next week (on Tuesday), and there is the risk surrounding the way the market is going to react to it," said Toshiyuki Suzuki, market economist at Sanwa Bank in London.
Japan's May current account surplus is forecast to jump to 962 billion yen from the previous 355 billion.
Elsewhere, the British pound continued to rise against the mark, surging to a new 70-month high of 2.9650 marks in late European trade. It was at 2.9580/90 marks late on Thursday.
Sterling/mark has been rising to new multi-year highs nearly every trading day since June 26, mainly on speculation that the Bank of England will raise interest rates in the near future.

The rally has been given additional impetus by the UK budget, unveiled on Wednesday, which the market perceived as not being stringent enough to curb consumer demand. This led to heightened speculation the BoE would have to hike rates to keep the economy under control.
